feedback: This candidate changes only kd, from 0.4 to 0.5, and restores base_speed to 1.5, which is the best raced setting. Iteration 1 (base_speed 1.5, kd 0.4) scored 170.5, the best so far. Iteration 2 showed that lowering base_speed to 1.3 cut the score to 86.8, with 0 oval finishes and more line losses on the s-bend (1.15) and slalom (1.15). Speed is therefore not the lever to pull. The kd step from 0.2 to 0.4 gave the largest gain in iterations 0 to 1, so a further small kd step is the next logical test. Geometry, kp 4.0, ki 0.2, sensor weights and line_loss (last_direction) are unchanged, so any difference can be attributed to kd. Judged from the earlier races and the contents alone, the candidate is valid and sits within the contract limits, and it is a single-variable step from the best raced design. Approve it so the race can show whether line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom fall, which the iteration 2 result already suggested is the main issue. Read the next race as follows. If line_loss_events fall and max_error drops below 0.06 on some runs, keep kd at 0.5 and consider a small base_speed rise toward 1.6 if completion_time is the limit. If steering_oscillation rises well above the 0.25 to 0.27 level while line losses persist, step kd back to 0.45 rather than changing kp. If the oval finishes more often but completion_time stays high, look for time gains from base_speed before touching geometry.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom fall below about 1.0 and max_error drops under 0.06 while progress still stalls, try base_speed 1.6 with kd 0.5 held, since speed 1.3 (iteration 2) was worse than 1.5 (iteration 1).

If steering_oscillation rises well above the iteration 1 level of about 0.27 while line losses persist, reduce kd to 0.45 rather than changing kp, since kd 0.2 to 0.4 improved the score from 69.5 to 170.5.
Keep kp 4.0, ki 0.2 and the geometry fixed for the next race, so that the kd effect stays separable from other changes.
